text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter tells reporters after talks in Abuja with military ruler General Sani Abacha that Nigeria's state elections due to hold in the second half of this year will now take place next year.
- United States remains the single biggest buyer of Nigerian crude oil, according to a central bank report just published.
- Federal government reaps 15 billion naira from valued added tax in the first five months of 1997, some 3.5 billion naira more than for the same year-ago period.

- For the third consecutive year, Nigeria attracts a special paragraph in annual report of International Labour Organisation, the group's mode of censuring members states considered culpable of gross human and trade union rights abuses.
- Opposition National Democratic Colaition says it has been invited by the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group on Nigeria to its July 10 meeting in London.

- Nigeria's Vision 2010 committee, which is planning the country's economic future has set for the nation a gross domestic product growth target of 10 percent provided an enabling environment is created.
- Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit is reviewing its 1997 expenditure because of government default in paying up its cash obligations to the company.
- Nigerian society of engineers warns of imminent collapse in electricity supply if enormous resources are not provided to rehabilitate facilities of the national power authority.
- Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter's bid to secure the release of political detainees fails.
- More than 20 million litres of petrol discharged in Lagos to end fuel scarcity in the area.
- Habib Bank Nigeria Limited seeks central bank's approval to introduce "Islamic" or interest-free banking in the country.
- Federal government earned more than 500 million naira from its privatised toll gates on highways last year, said works minister Major-General Abdulkareem Adisa.
